questions.text: What is LATERAL used for on a subquery in FROM?

answers.text: To let the subquery reference columns from preceding FROM items
To automatically materialize a CTE
To forbid correlation
To create an index

questions.explanation: Without LATERAL, a FROM subquery is evaluated independently of neighboring FROM items; LATERAL allows correlation with preceding items.

questions.text: What does WITH ORDINALITY add to the result of a table function?

answers.text: A bigint column numbering rows starting from 1
A UUID for each row
The table OID
The current transaction ID

questions.explanation: WITH ORDINALITY adds an ordinal column to the result of a table function.

questions.text: What do GROUPING SETS, CUBE, and ROLLUP do?

answers.text: They allow multiple grouping variants to be computed in one query
They create physical table partitions
They change the isolation level
They enable parallel query

questions.explanation: Section 7.2.4 describes more complex grouping operations using grouping sets.

It turns any SELECT into a trigger
It forbids UNION

questions.text: Where are window function calls directly allowed?

answers.text: In the SELECT list and ORDER BY
In WHERE and GROUP BY
Only in HAVING
Only in FROM

questions.explanation: Window functions are evaluated after WHERE/GROUP BY/HAVING, so they are directly allowed in SELECT and ORDER BY.

questions.text: What does an expression index provide?

answers.text: It indexes the result of an expression rather than only the original column value
It automatically creates a materialized view
It changes the column type
It disables the planner

questions.explanation: Chapter 11 separately covers indexes on expressions.

It indexes only half of the columns by position
It exists only inside a transaction

questions.text: What does `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` do compared with plain EXPLAIN?

answers.text: It actually executes the query and reports actual timing/row counts together with the plan
It only parses SQL without planning
It automatically creates an index
It always rolls back DML

questions.explanation: Section 14.1.2 describes executing the query to collect actual runtime characteristics.

questions.text: Which isolation level does PostgreSQL use by default?

answers.text: Read Committed
Serializable
Read Uncommitted
Always Repeatable Read

questions.explanation: Read Committed is PostgreSQL's default isolation level.

questions.text: Which statements about LATERAL are true?

answers.text: A LATERAL subquery can reference preceding FROM items
For a table function, the LATERAL keyword is optional when its arguments already reference preceding items
LEFT JOIN LATERAL is useful when the source row must be preserved even if the right side returns no rows
LATERAL is forbidden inside a JOIN tree

questions.explanation: Section 7.2.1.5 describes correlated FROM items and examples of LEFT JOIN LATERAL.

questions.text: Which statements about a window frame are true?

answers.text: A frame can be smaller than the entire partition
With ORDER BY, the default frame runs from the start of the partition through the current row and its peers
Without ORDER BY, the default frame includes all rows in the partition
PARTITION BY always makes the frame exactly one row

questions.explanation: The window-function introduction separately explains the window frame and its defaults.

questions.text: Which of the following features relate to PostgreSQL indexes?

answers.text: Multicolumn indexes
Indexes on expressions
Partial indexes
Index-only scans / covering indexes
SAVEPOINT

questions.explanation: PostgreSQL supports multicolumn indexes, indexes on expressions, partial indexes, and index-only scans with covering indexes.

source.locator: Multicolumn, expression, partial, and covering indexes

questions.text: Which statements about EXPLAIN plans are true?

answers.text: The planner can choose a Seq Scan, Index Scan, or Bitmap Scan depending on cost
A condition not supported by the chosen index can be applied as a Filter
ORDER BY can sometimes be satisfied by index order without a separate Sort
The presence of an index forces the planner to always use it

questions.explanation: EXPLAIN examples show the choice among scan nodes, Filter conditions, and use of index ordering.

questions.text: Which statements about isolation and locking are true?

answers.text: Read Committed, Repeatable Read, and Serializable are treated as isolation levels
PostgreSQL supports explicit table and row locks
Deadlocks are discussed separately
Any lock automatically means a deadlock

questions.explanation: Chapter 13 separates isolation levels, explicit locking, and deadlocks.

questions.text: Which statements about recursive CTEs in PostgreSQL are true?

answers.text: They are written using WITH RECURSIVE
A recursive query can specify search order
A recursive query can track cycles
A recursive CTE must modify data

questions.explanation: Recursive CTEs use WITH RECURSIVE; PostgreSQL also supports search-order control and cycle detection.

questions.text: Which statements about CTE materialization are true?

answers.text: A CTE can be materialized separately from the outer query
The materialization choice can affect whether the CTE and outer query can be optimized together
Every CTE is always physically stored forever
WITH disables the optimizer

questions.explanation: CTE materialization can separate its evaluation from the outer query and therefore affect joint optimization.

questions.text: Which operations can use `ONLY` to restrict an inheritance operation to the parent table?

answers.text: SELECT
UPDATE
DELETE
COMMIT

questions.explanation: SELECT, UPDATE, and DELETE support ONLY to restrict the operation to the specified parent table.

questions.text: Which statements about EXPLAIN ANALYZE with data-modifying commands are true?

answers.text: The command is actually executed
If changes must not be persisted, the safe pattern requires an explicit transaction followed by ROLLBACK
EXPLAIN ANALYZE automatically rolls back every command
EXPLAIN ANALYZE never executes triggers

questions.explanation: Because ANALYZE actually executes the statement, data-modifying commands require care.
